question: Built by joining the 5' phosphate of one nucleotide to the 3' hydroxyl of the next, a _____ is a chain with a direction as well as a sequence.
questions: Four drugs approved for Duchenne muscular dystrophy work by making the splicing machinery skip an exon, which is a _____ used as a medicine rather than as information.
At up to 455 exabytes per gram and stable for millennia, a _____ is being developed as a storage medium for ordinary computer files.
abstract:
The nucleic acids, DNA and RNA, are the principal informational molecules of the cell, deoxyribonucleic acid having the unique role of genetic material and the several kinds of ribonucleic acid taking part in a range of cellular activities. RNA is not only informational, since in present-day cells it also catalyses reactions, among them steps of protein synthesis and of RNA processing. Both are polymers of nucleotides, each a purine or pyrimidine base linked to a phosphorylated sugar, ribose in RNA and deoxyribose in DNA. The chain is built by phosphodiester bonds between the 5' phosphate of one nucleotide and the 3' hydroxyl of another, so it has a direction as well as a sequence, and it is always synthesised and written from the 5' end towards the 3'. A short chain is an oligonucleotide; the polynucleotides making up cellular RNA and DNA run to thousands and to millions of units respectively.

Short chains made deliberately are now medicines, and antisense oligonucleotides work by binding a target transcript and redirecting how it is spliced or how much of it survives. Four such drugs are approved in the United States for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, eteplirsen, golodirsen, viltolarsen and casimersen, each making the splicing machinery skip an exon so that some dystrophin is made. Small interfering RNAs work differently again, intercepting genetic information in transit rather than altering the genome, which has taken them from a niche technique to the routine management of chronic conditions. The molecule is also being taken out of biology altogether, since DNA offers an information density of up to 455 exabytes per gram and stability over thousands of years. What has held that back is not writing the data but reading a chosen part of it back, and electric fields are one way now being used to address stored strands individually.
